reasoning.overall: Spain face Peru in a World Cup warm-up at Estadio Cuauhtémoc in Puebla, Mexico. Key news: Lamine Yamal and Nico Williams have been left out of Spain's squad for this match, reducing their most dynamic wide attackers. However, Spain's squad depth remains extraordinary — Rodri, Zubimendi, Pedri, Olmo, Cubarsí, Laporte, Grimaldo, Cucurella form a world-class core. Peru's recent form is mixed (4W-3D-3L), with losses to Chile (twice) and Senegal, and they struggle against top opposition. Spain's statistical profile (68% possession, 17.7 shots, 6.7 on target avg) dwarfs Peru's (50% possession, 8.4 shots, 2.7 on target). Even without Yamal/Williams, Spain should dominate possession and create multiple high-quality chances. Peru's best hope is a counter-attack goal via Carrillo or Ugarriza. The venue in Mexico gives Peru slight regional familiarity but not a true home advantage. Spain's recent friendly draws vs Iraq and Egypt suggest they can be complacent in low-stakes matches, so a draw has non-trivial probability, but the quality gap is large enough that Spain wins most scenarios.
reasoning.t1_result: Spain's win probability is dominant (~0.65) due to overwhelming squad quality and tactical superiority even minus Yamal and Williams. Peru has a small home-ish edge (~0.15) from Latin American venue familiarity and counter-attacking threat. Draw (~0.20) reflects Spain's recent friendly complacency and the low-stakes context. Headline score 1-2: Spain scores twice through midfield dominance and set-piece quality; Peru grabs one on a counter.
reasoning.t2_player: Spain lineup without Yamal/Williams: Olmo and Ferrán Torres fill the wide roles, Oyarzabal as central striker. Rodri-Zubimendi-Pedri midfield trio controls tempo. Peru: Gallese in goal, Carrillo as wide threat, Ugarriza up front, Yotún and Noriega in midfield. Peru's 4-2-3-1 aims to stay compact and counter; Spain's 4-3-3 will pin Peru deep with possession and pressing.
reasoning.t3_events: Spain likely scores first between minutes 20-40 through sustained build-up or a Grimaldo/Cucurella overlap. Peru's best chance comes from a Carrillo counter around minutes 45-65. Spain's second goal likely arrives in minutes 60-80 as fatigue opens space. Few cards expected in a friendly; Peru may commit tactical fouls to slow Spain's rhythm.
reasoning.t4_stats: Spain will dominate possession (~65%) and passing accuracy (~90%) with their technical midfield. Shots favor Spain heavily (~16 vs ~6) with ~6 on target vs ~2. Peru will commit more fouls (~14 vs ~10) trying to disrupt Spain's flow. Corners favor Spain (~7 vs ~3) from sustained attacking pressure. Peru's GK Gallese will face more saves (~4 vs ~1). Defensive actions higher for Peru (~28 vs ~18) as they spend most of the match without the ball.
